name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+32 partisan lean makes a Republican win improbable
Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but Democratic nominee holds a large financial edge
No public polling; Republican nominee shows minimal fundraising
model.rationale: The district's D+32 fundamentals dominate everything else here: even with Espaillat off the ballot, the Democratic nominee enters with roughly $1.6 million raised and nearly $1.9 million in outside backing against a Republican with no visible fundraising. Markets price Democrats near certain, and nothing in the evidence suggests moving materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late scandal involving the Democratic nominee or a sudden influx of Republican outside spending could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-13, covering upper Manhattan and parts of the Bronx, is among the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country. Adriano Espaillat lost renomination, so the seat is open, but Democratic nominee Darializa Avila Chevalier enters the general election with a large financial advantage. She has raised about $1.6 million and drawn roughly $1.9 million in outside support, while Republican Jomo Williams shows little fundraising activity.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Polymarket puts Democratic chances around 96 percent. The open seat and lack of polling add some uncertainty, but the district's D+32 lean points to a solid Democratic win in the mid-to-high twenties.
